We will be launching more exciting activities in the future. Thank you for your attention. PCBWay’s Open Source Community is a platform of sharing creative electronic projects and insightful knowledge for global makers. “Learning from each other and making progress together” is the community atmosphere we want to create. Now a direct channel to express your own ideas about electronics and receive feedback from the community is ready for you! Whenever you have some useful and practical tips on how to design or make an E-projects, or anything that you think should be discussed at PCBWay, you’re always welcome to post it at our community. Come and be a valuable partner of us! How to submit? There are currently 2 types of submission of your contributing articles. Type A: Submit articles at PCBWay You’re encouraged to share the knowledge about PCB design tips, software instructions, step-by-step tutorials, or any basics needed for new learners to get their first boards being designed. Just submit your article directly through the following form. [Submit your post] Content requirement: Project making and sharing, electronic technical discussions, and so on. Rewards: --PCBWay will reward contributors with $10 - $50 coupon & 400 - 800 PCBWay Beans within 7 work days. --Every “PCBWayer” will be awarded honorary titles (according to the number of published articles, popularity and quality, etc). Silver writer (N<5); Golden writer (5<N<15), 2% off for PCB orders Diamond writer (N>15), 5% off for PCB orders N=The cumulative number of articles contributed --Have the opportunity to be published in other large magazines/websites. Type B: Submit articles on other platforms You can also post the articles related to PCBWay on your own website or other open source platforms<dynamic-value> instructable, hackaday, hackster.io etc. Workflow: Share the articles on your social media (Facebook, ins, twitter, LinkedIn), then tag @PCBWay. ﻿Content requirements: ❖ Original content related to PCBWay includes but not limited to review, unboxing, project sharing, promotion, etc. ❖ Add at least one more PCBWay link. ❖ At least 3 pictures. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for FreeCAD PCBWay Plug-In for FreeCAD by: Anson Jul 29,2022 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in CNC Machining FreeCAD CNC machining 3D printing Sheet metal Injection molding Send your 3D design to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. PCBWay's 3D & CNC services always well received by our customers. Now we have an in-depth cooperation with FreeCAD. FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D modeler made primarily to design real-life objects of any size. It is widely used among engineers. Now when you complete the 3D design on FreeCAD, you can place an order on PCBWay with just one click. FreeCAD will pass step files to us. You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files (usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before production. Installation from the official FreeCAD tools Just click the "tools" ----“Addon manager”---Choose the "PCBWay” from the selection list, click and install it. Manual installation You can also download the latest file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-FreeCAD , then click the "Macro", put the python file in the path, and click the “execute“ As a sponsor of FreeCAD, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > Countersink & Counterbore Holes Design Guidelines Countersink & Counterbore Holes Design Guidelines by: Mila Sep 07,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in Countersink & Counterbore This design guide provides structural engineers and mechanical designers with essential Design for Manufacturability (DFM) rules for Countersink (CSINK) and Counterbore (CBORE) holes in sheet metal fabrication and CNC machining. Following these geometric standards helps prevent knife-edge cutting, material tearing, bolt head protrusion, and engineering question (EQ) delays—ensuring a 100% first-pass review rate and fast delivery schedules. 1. Countersink (CSINK) vs. Counterbore (CBORE) Hole Explained When designing parts for flush or recessed fasteners, choosing the correct hole geometry is critical to achieving functional performance and clean aesthetics. Countersink Hole (CSINK): A conical basin cut into the surface to accept flat-head or undercut countersunk screws. The primary goal is to seat the screw head completely flush with or slightly below the outer surface of the part. Counterbore Hole (CBORE): A flat-bottomed, cylindrical enlargement of a hole designed to accommodate cylindrical screw heads, such as Socket Head Cap Screws (SHCS), allowing the fastener to sink entirely below the material surface. 2. Countersink Angle Standards: Metric vs. Imperial A common cause of assembly interference is pairing screws with the wrong countersink angle. Always align your CAD design with the corresponding thread standard: 90° Angle (Metric Standard): The universal standard for all Metric countersunk screws (e.g., M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6 per DIN 965 / ISO 7046). 82° Angle (Imperial/US Standard): The standard angle for Unified National Thread fasteners in North America (e.g., #4-40, #6-32, #8-32, 1/4"-20 UNC). 100° Angle (Aero & Thin Sheet Special): Used primarily in aerospace applications and ultra-thin sheet metal where shallow fastener heads are required to prevent punch-through. 3. Sheet Metal Countersinking: Critical DFM Rules Processing countersinks on laser-cut sheet metal requires strict adherence to sheet thickness limits and feature clearances. Rule 1: The "Knife-Edge" & Minimum Material Margin Never allow a countersink to cut entirely through a piece of sheet metal. Leaving zero cylindrical wall thickness creates a razor-thin knife-edge at the bottom of the hole, leading to burrs, tool chatter, hole enlargement, and structural tearing during assembly. Minimum Web Thickness: Always preserve a straight cylindrical wall height of at least 0.50 mm (0.020") at the bottom of the countersink. Maximum Countersink Depth: The countersink head depth (H_cs) should not exceed 60% to 70% of the total sheet thickness (T). Max Depth (H_cs) ≤ 0.70 × T (Note: If sheet thickness is less than the countersink depth, evaluate using Press/Dimpled Countersinks or PEM Clinch Studs instead.) Rule 2: Edge Distance & Bend Clearance Tensile forces during bending can deform nearby countersunk holes, preventing flat-head screws from sitting flush. Distance to Edge: The distance from the hole axis to the plate edge must be ≥ 2.0 × Major Countersink Diameter (D_major). Distance to Bend Line: The edge of the countersink rim must be placed at a distance ≥ (1/2 × Bend Die Opening + 2 × T) away from any fold lines. 4. CNC Machined Countersink & Counterbore Hole Depth Rules For solid CNC-milled parts, tool access and clearance tolerances dictate design quality. CBORE Diameter Clearance: Always size the counterbore diameter (D_cbore) 0.5 mm to 1.0 mm (0.020" to 0.040") larger than the actual screw head diameter to allow for socket driver clearance and anodizing/plating thickness. CBORE Depth Margin: Model the counterbore depth 0.2 mm to 0.4 mm deeper than the screw head height. This ensures the screw sits slightly below the surface, even with manufacturing tolerances on the fastener itself. 5. Recommended Countersink & Counterbore Drill Size Chart Use the following standard dimensions when modeling 3D CAD geometries for Metric and Imperial fasteners: Metric Standards (90° Countersink / Standard Counterbore) Imperial Standards (82° Countersink / Standard Counterbore) 6. CAD Modeling & 2D Drawing Setup 1. 3D CAD Representation: Model physical conical or cylindrical cuts directly in your STEP/IGES solid models matching the exact values in the size chart above. 2. 2D Drawing Callouts: Clearly annotate hole specifications using standard ANSI/ISO symbols: Countersink Symbol: v (e.g., DIA 4.5 THRU, CSINK DIA 8.6 x 90°) Counterbore Symbol: u (e.g., DIA 4.5 THRU, CBORE DIA 7.5 DEPTH 4.4) 3. Plating & Coating Allowances: If specifying thick powder coatings (60–120 µm), enlarge the CBORE diameter by an extra 0.2 mm or specify masking on the engineering drawing. 7. Pre-Manufacturing Checklist Before submitting your CAD files for quotation, verify the following design details: Angle Matching Verified: Metric flat-head screws are specified with 90° countersinks; Imperial screws are specified with 82° countersinks. No Knife-Edges: Plate thickness exceeds countersink depth, leaving at least 0.50 mm of straight wall stock. Edge Distance Clear: Countersink rim to sheet edge is ≥ 2.0 × D_major. Tool Driver Room: Counterbore diameters provide adequate clearance for socket heads and wrench tools. Drawing Symbols Correct: 2D drawings contain explicit depth and diameter callouts. Verify Now Blog > Hardware Installation Design Guidelines Hardware Installation Design Guidelines by: Mila Sep 07,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in Hardware insertion Hardware installation adds threaded connection points, mounting features, and structural support directly to sheet metal parts. It is especially useful for thin sheet metal that is difficult to tap, applications where access to the back side is limited, and assemblies that require repeatable fastening. This guide covers key design considerations for sheet metal parts with press-fit or self-clinching (PEM) hardware, including hardware selection, mounting hole and spacing engineering data, edge clearance, bend clearance, load direction, and production file preparation standards. 1. Hardware Options and Selection Choosing the right hardware depends on how the finished part will be assembled and loaded. Self-Clinching Nuts Self-clinching nuts provide permanent internal threads in sheet metal parts. They are a practical alternative to tapping when the sheet is too thin to provide sufficient thread engagement. Common Applications: Electronic enclosures, control panels, mounting brackets, equipment housings, structural sheet metal assemblies. Typical Series: S/SS Series (standard steel), CLS Series (for stainless steel), SP Series (for corrosion-resistant hard stainless steel). Self-Clinching Studs Self-clinching studs provide a permanent threaded shaft extending from the sheet metal surface. They are useful when another component needs to be positioned over or mounted onto the sheet. Typical Applications: Panel mounting, PCB mounting, electrical assemblies, brackets and supports. Typical Series: FH (flush-head type), FHS (stainless steel type), TFH (thin-sheet type). Standoffs Standoffs create a fixed spacing between two components while providing a threaded mounting point. Common Applications: PCB mounting, electronic enclosures, multi-layer assemblies, panel-to-panel mounting. Typical Series: BSO (thru-hole threaded), SOO (blind threaded), CSOS (concealed-head type). Flush Hardware Flush or low-profile hardware is used when the installed fastener needs to remain close to or completely level with the sheet surface. Note that the final installed height varies depending on hardware type and sheet material. Always check specific hardware specifications before finalizing the design. 2. Core Design Rules and Industry Engineering Reference Data Before laying out mounting holes, general Design for Manufacturability (DFM) rules should be combined with fastener catalogs (such as PEM standards). Minimum Edge Distance (Center-to-Edge Distance) Hardware installed too close to an edge can weaken the sheet around the mounting point and cause the sheet edge to bulge or deform during installation or under load. Engineering Rules of Thumb: Rule Formula: Distance from the mounting hole center to the nearest edge C ≥ 1.5 × Dh (where Dh is the mounting hole diameter). Standard Recommendation: Check "Min. Distance to Edge" in PEM catalogs. For high-load or thin-sheet applications, C ≥ 2.0 × Dh is recommended. Minimum Hole-to-Hole Spacing Adjacent hardware holes positioned too closely can cause cumulative stress deformation and weaken the sheet metal between holes. Identical Hardware: Recommended center-to-center distance S ≥ 3 × Dh. Different Hardware Types: Follow the larger clearance requirement and ensure installation tooling envelopes do not intersect (installation anvil diameter is typically 3-5mm larger than the hole). Bend Line Clearance Bending creates a plastic deformation zone (bend allowance area) around the bend. Installing hardware inside or too close to this area can cause tooling interference during forming or distort the mounting hole. Clearance Formula (Hole center to bend tangent line): L_bend ≥ R + t + C_margin Where R is inner bend radius, t is sheet thickness, and C_margin is safety margin (typically 1.5 to 2 times fastener flange radius, or maintaining center distance to bend line at 2t + R + 3mm or greater). 3. Load Direction and Material Compatibility Load Direction Principle (Push-out vs. Pull-out) Self-clinching fasteners rely on knurling and clinician grooves pressed into sheet metal for cold-flow bonding, resulting in significant differences in retention strength along different axes. Nuts: Applied load must pull the nut into the sheet metal (Push-out force direction). Never apply bolt tension that directly pulls the nut out of the sheet (Pull-out force). Studs: Tightening force should press the stud head firmly against the sheet surface, avoiding direct axial tension pulling the stud out from the back. Sheet Hardness and Material Matching Successful clinch insertion requires the fastener material to be harder than the base sheet metal so that the knurled teeth can cold-extrude into the sheet. Aluminum Alloys (e.g., 5052-H32 / 6061-T6): Compatible with carbon steel (S series) or stainless steel (CLS series) fasteners. Recommended sheet hardness: HRB 50 max. Cold-Rolled Steel / Galvanized Steel (SPCC/SECC): Use carbon steel (S series) or hardened stainless steel fasteners. Recommended sheet hardness: HRB 80 max. Stainless Steel (e.g., 304 / 316): Hardened stainless steel fasteners (such as PEM SP series) must be used. Standard CLS stainless fasteners cannot extrude into 304 sheets. Recommended sheet hardness: HRB 88/90 max. 4. Surface Finishing and Installation Sequence Surface treatments (powder coating, plating, anodizing) significantly affect hardware installation and should follow these engineering guidelines: 5. File Preparation Requirements (CAD/DFM) 2D DXF/DWG Files: Maintain 1:1 scale, remove duplicate lines, construction geometry, and open contours. Draw hardware mounting holes directly at the manufacturer's recommended standard diameter (Dh) without manual scaling. 3D STEP/STP/IGES Models: Cloud Manufacturing Platforms (e.g., SCS, Xometry): Remove 3D hardware fastener models from exported STEP files, leaving only exact mounting holes to prevent automated DFM algorithms from misinterpreting fasteners as complex CNC milling features. Traditional Engineering Drawings: Call out fastener BOM part numbers, specifications (e.g., PEM S-M4-1), and installation faces on assembly drawings. 6. Hardware Installation Design Checklist Hardware type and thread size selected, with sheet hardness verified below fastener hardness limits (e.g., SP series for stainless steel). Mounting hole size matches specifications, with edge distance C ≥ 1.5 × Dh (≥ 6.4 mm recommended). Hole center to bend tangent line distance meets L_bend ≥ 2t + R + 3mm. Load direction verified to pull hardware into sheet (Push-out direction) rather than pulling it out. Installation area is accessible by tooling, free from interfering deep pockets, tight flanges, or narrow channels. Insertion sequence coordinated with powder coating/anodizing/plating processes. 3D STEP files prepared with hardware solids removed, leaving accurate mounting hole geometry. Be Part of the PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest! by: PCBWay Sep 03,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News We are glad to announce that PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest has arrived. Prior to this, PCBWay successfully held six design contests. In each contest, we saw many eye-catching projects shared by outstanding and creative electronic engineers and enthusiasts. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest will continue the previous purpose, which is to encourage more and more people to explore the charm of electronic design and participate in it. PCBWay 7th Project Design Contest: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . In this contest, in addition to the two themes of Electronic Project and Mechanical Project that have appeared before, we also introduced STM32 Project, hoping to give designers more room to perform. The contest will start on September 2nd, 2024, and project submissions will be accepted until January 19th, 2025. After this, the judging phase will begin, and the final winners will be announced on the PCBWay Blog on March 10th, 2025. Two ways to participate in the contest: Go to the contest page, find the Participate Now button and click it. In this case, the submitted project will automatically be entered into the competition; participants only need to select the theme of entry. Please note that if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. After filling in all the project information, simply click "Submit" at the bottom of the page. Go to the SharedProject Community ( https://www.pcbway.com/project/shareproject/ ) and click Create a project. Select the theme you are going to participate in. Similarly, if you are submitting a mechanical project, please switch to the CNC |3D Printing Project page. Hint: Sharing complete project files, including Gerber, BOM, Centroid file, schematics, 3D files, and so on will increase the chances of receiving a higher score. Awards and corresponding prizes: The First Prize : 1 winner, $1500 Cash + $200 Coupon + A Palm-sized Robot Dog*1 The Second Prize : 2 winners, $1000 Cash + $100 Coupon + Raspberry Pi 5 4GB *1 The Third Prize : 3 winners, $500 Cash + $50 Coupon + OpenMV4 H7 R2 Cam Smart Camera *1 Popular Design Prize : 10 winners, $100 Cash + $20 Coupon + $10 3D Printing Coupon + Multimeter ZTY890DPro *1 Participation Prize : Raspberry Pi Pico * 1 STM32 Great Project Prize : Six-Claw Multifunctional Aluminum Alloy Soldering Table *1 For more detailed information about the contest, please refer to: https://www.pcbway.com/activity/7th-project-design-contest.html . If there are any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment below.We wish you the best of luck and look forward to your innovative designs! Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Importers are responsible for exercising reasonable care in calculating applicable tariffs to their products based on all applicable legal authorities and correctly declaring the amount to CBP on entry documentation. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Update on June 24th Current Tax Rates for Various PCBWay Products Bare PCBs : 55% Stencils : 98% SMT Services : 45% CNC Machining : 65% Aluminum & Steel Components : 73% Plastic Components : 65% Other Products : 55% Note: The above tax rates are estimated for reference only, as tax rates are subject to significant real-time fluctuations. The dividing line between formal and informal customs declaration is 2500 In response to recent changes, we currently recommends the following logistics options: We advise using DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) logistics services with prepaid tariffs, such as: 1. DHL DTP (Duty & Tax Prepaid) , SF express If the item falls under HTS codes 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 10% tariff exemption. However, DHL may incorrectly apply duties. If the recipient is charged duties despite the exemption, dispute it with DHL immediately—delays may invalidate the claim. DHL DTP will prepay customs duties & taxes. DHL may contact recipients for required documentation/clarification to clear shipments (regardless of Incoterm® used). Download POA form: [POA form.pdf] Due to tariff uncertainty, we will apply a 30%~73%duty rate (current U.S. rates: 30%~73%%, with a 10% exemption for 9903.01.32/33). If the final duty rate is lower than 30%~73%, we will refund the difference upon receiving the tax invoice. For questions, contact: logistics@pcbway.com 2. FedEx-IP(DDP), Fedex-FICP (DDP – Delivered Duty Paid) FedEx DDP service will prepay customs duties & taxes. Providing an EIN or SSN will help expedite customs clearance. We recommend recipients prepare and email the 5106 Form to paperwork@fedex.com (include the tracking number in the email subject). Download forms: [5106 Form.pdf] & [PCB Worksheet.pdf] Due to tariff uncertainty, we will apply a 30%~73% duty rate. For questions, contact: logistics@pcbway.com 3. Global Direct Shipping Duties included in shipping costs. Maximum declared value per package: The logistics provider does not accept U.S.-bound shipments with a declared value exceeding $60 USD (inclusive). Global Direct Shipping is likely the most cost-effective option. Duties are included in the shipping cost, avoiding unexpected fees. Best for lower-value shipments (max declared value: $60 USD per package). No need for additional tax disputes or refund processes. If your shipment meets the value limit, this is the simplest and most economical choice. 4. Global Standard Shipping, USPS Prepaid tax fee: A 30% duty rate (based on declared value) will be charged upon package arrival. No refunds, no additional charges, and no tax invoice provided. For further inquiries, please contact: logistics@pcbway.com Update on May 12th The Government of the United States of America (the “United States”) and the Government of the People’s Republic of China (“China”), Recognizing the importance of their bilateral economic and trade relationship to both countries and the global economy; Recognizing the importance of a sustainable, long-term, and mutually beneficial economic and trade relationship; Reflecting on their recent discussions and believing that continued discussions have the potential to address the concerns of each side in their economic and trade relationship; and Moving forward in the spirit of mutual opening, continued communication, cooperation, and mutual respect; The Parties commit to take the following actions by May 14, 2025 : The United States will (i) modify the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of China (including articles of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macau Special Administrative Region) set forth in Executive Order 14257 of April 2, 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles pursuant to the terms of said Order; and (ii) removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Executive Order 14259 of April 8, 2025 and Executive Order 14266 of April 9, 2025. China will (i) modify accordingly the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of the United States set forth in Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 4 of 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining additional ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles, and removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 5 of 2025 and Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 6 of 2025; and (ii) adopt all necessary administrative measures to suspend or remove the non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since April 2, 2025. After taking the aforementioned actions, the Parties will establish a mechanism to continue discussions about economic and trade relations. The representative from the Chinese side for these discussions will be He Lifeng, Vice Premier of the State Council, and the representatives from the U.S. side will be Scott Bessent, Secretary of the Treasury, and Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative. These discussions may be conducted alternately in China and the United States, or a third country upon agreement of the Parties. As required, the two sides may conduct working-level consultations on relevant economic and trade issues. https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/05/joint-statement-on-u-s-china-economic-and-trade-meeting-in-geneva/ Updated on April 25th **Presidential Executive Order on Tariff Adjustments for Chinese Goods** On April 8, 2025 (local time), U.S. President Donald Trump issued an executive order announcing the following tariff measures on goods originating from China (including Hong Kong, China): 1. **Elimination of De Minimis Exemption for Chinese-origin Goods** 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the tariff exemption is 125%) Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** 3.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. 4.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. Details: On February 3, 2025 (Eastern Time), the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) announced additional tariffs on imported products originating from China (including Hong Kong). Regardless of their value, all covered imported products will be assessed, and shipments containing such goods will no longer be eligible for the "de minimis" duty and tax exemption under 19 U.S.C. § 1321(a)(2)(C). The United States will impose an additional 10% tariff on all products from China (including the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region). The executive order imposing additional tariffs officially took effect at 12:01 AM Eastern Standard Time on February 4, 2025. Shipments arriving after this time or declared for arrival after this time are subject to the order. The "$800 de minimis exemption" and the "T86 clearance model" no longer apply.As a result, shipments from PCBWay to the U.S. will incur additional tariffs. We will continue to optimize our website and services to provide a better experience in response to this situation. Note: Since this policy has just started, the express delivery may be chaotic. The event will take place from September 9 to 11, 2026, at Songdo Convensia in Incheon, South Korea. During the exhibition, PCBWay will be at Booth R310, where visitors can meet our team, learn more about our PCB and electronics manufacturing capabilities, and discuss solutions for their upcoming projects. About KPCA Show 2026 KPCA Show 2026, officially known as the International Semiconductor Circuits and Advanced Packaging Show, will be held at Songdo Convensia in Incheon from September 9 to 11, 2026. The exhibition is organized by the Korea Semiconductor Packaging and Circuits Association (KPCA) and Incheon Metropolitan City. The show brings together companies and professionals from across the electronics manufacturing industry, with exhibition areas covering advanced semiconductor substrates, semiconductor packaging, plating and surface treatment, reliability equipment, automotive electronics, and motion control and collaborative robotics. As PCB technology continues to evolve toward higher density, greater reliability, and increasingly complex applications, KPCA Show provides an opportunity for industry professionals to explore new technologies and connect with manufacturing partners. Meet PCBWay at Booth R310 At Booth R310, the PCBWay team will be available to introduce our manufacturing capabilities and discuss how we can support projects from prototype development to production. PCBWay provides a range of electronics manufacturing services, including: PCB fabrication PCB assembly HDI and rigid-flex PCB Flexible PCB Advanced PCB manufacturing CNC machining 3D printing Sheet metal fabrication Injection molding Box build assembly Whether you are developing a new electronic product, preparing prototypes, or looking for a manufacturing partner for larger-scale production, our team can discuss your project requirements and help identify suitable manufacturing solutions. Visit PCBWay at KPCA Show 2026 If you are attending KPCA Show 2026, we invite you to stop by and meet the PCBWay team. Meet PCBWay at electronica 2024! by: PCBWay Oct 18,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Once again, we welcome the famous technology event electronica in Munich, Germany! Since the first exhibition was held in 1964, electronica has gradually grown and now covers the entire world of electronics, including the micro- and nano-worlds of semiconductor and micro systems technology, as well as measurement and sensor technology, display technology and vehicle electronics, etc., which is the best choice for any technology enthusiasts and industry practitioners. PCBWay has participated in theelectronica many times and has received a warm response every time. At the exhibition, everyone has the opportunity to get close to our various products and fully evaluate the performance and quality of our products, which is far beyond the scope of online communication. On-site interaction gives us the opportunity to answer everyone's questions in a timely manner and help them understand the products more comprehensively, thereby accelerating the process of cooperation. Therefore, after the exhibition, we not only strengthened our cooperation with existing customers, but also successfully attracted the attention of many new potential partners. PCBWay will certainly not be absent from this year's exhibition.In addition, in order to give everyone a better exhibition experience and also to show how much importance PCBWay attaches to this exhibition, this year we made some innovations: Time: 2024.11.12-2024.11.15 Location: Trade Fair Center Messe München, Germany PCBWay Booth No.: A1.163 Highlights: Color- printed Boards In addition to the PCB series products, 3D printed parts and sheet metal parts that we have been displaying in the past, we will also bring the latest color-printed board samples. This new product has attracted the attention and interest of many customers, so we hope to take this opportunity to let everyone experience the excellent effect and quality of the color-printed board in person. New Booth We focused on designing the on-site booth as well. We expanded the booth area to 5m x 14m, providing a larger activity space, and also improved the sophistication of various details, in order to make the overall atmosphere more professional and make everyone's visiting experience more comfortable. The final booth design renderings are as follows: Gifts We will also bring some small gifts to the exhibition, including water cups, neck masks, and T-shirts. Welcome to come and get them! Map: Also, we've prepared some free tickets, click the link and apply for them! https://tickets.messe-muenchen.de/MM/ELE24/Register/PCBWay_2024 Sorry, the 100+ current tickets are "sold out". We welcome you to our booth to receive gifts PCBWay will continue the past successful experience, bring more innovative products and solutions. We welcome you to visit our booth and witness PCBWay's innovation and growth! We’ve got everything ready, just wait for your arrival. ;) Exhibition Moments Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Join us Wanna be a dedicated PCBWay writer? Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Note: If you want to place an assembly order, please be sure to add MPN information to the BOM. This can help the quoter source the devices you need more accurately. Manual installation Except for the way mentioned before, you can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Fabrication-Toolkit-for-KiCad: Open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About BOM Through BOM files, we can get all information of the components used in your design. In order to speed up the quotation process, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) If you have more suggestions, please leave a message below, PCBWay has committed to providing everyone with high-quality services. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Join us Wanna be a dedicated PCBWay writer? We definately look forward to having you with us. pcbnew.EXCELLON_WRITER(self.board) drlwriter.SetOptions( False, True, self.board.GetDesignSettings().GetAuxOrigin(), False) drlwriter.SetFormat(False) drlwriter.CreateDrillandMapFilesSet(self.pctl.GetPlotDirName(), True, False) netlist_writer = pcbnew.IPC356D_WRITER(self.board) netlist_writer.Write(os.path.join(temp_dir, netlistFilename)) def get_components_file(self, temp_dir): if hasattr(self.board, 'GetModules'): footprints = list(self.board.GetModules()) else: footprints = list(self.board.GetFootprints()) footprints.sort(key=lambda x: x.GetReference()) for i, f in enumerate(footprints): try: footprint_name = str(f.GetFPID().GetFootprintName()) except AttributeError: footprint_name = str(f.GetFPID().GetLibItemName()) layer = { pcbnew.F_Cu: 'top', pcbnew.B_Cu: 'bottom', }.get(f.GetLayer()) f_attrs = f.GetAttributes() parsed_attrs = self.parse_attrs(f_attrs) mount_type = 'smt' if parsed_attrs['smd'] else 'tht' placed = not parsed_attrs['not_in_bom'] rotation = f.GetOrientation().AsDegrees() if hasattr(f.GetOrientation(), 'AsDegrees') else f.GetOrientation() / 10.0 designator = f.GetReference() pos_x = (f.GetPosition()[0] - self.board.GetDesignSettings().GetAuxOrigin()[0]) / 1000000.0 pos_y = (f.GetPosition()[1] - self.board.GetDesignSettings().GetAuxOrigin()[1]) * -1.0 / 1000000.0 mpn = self.get_mpn_from_footprint(f) pack = self.get_pack_from_footprint(f) if pack: footprint_name = pack value = f.GetValue() self.components.append({ 'pos_x': pos_x, 'pos_y': pos_y, 'rotation': rotation, is_exist_bom == False and placed == True: self.bom.append({ 'designator': designator, 'quantity': 1, 'value': value, 'pack': footprint_name, 'mpn': mpn, 'mount_type': mount_type }) if len(self.components) > 0: with open((os.path.join(temp_dir, positionsFilename)), 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as outfile: csvobj = csv.writer(outfile) in component['designator']): csvobj.writerow(component.values()) def get_gerber_parameter(self): boardWidth = pcbnew.ToMM(self.board.GetBoardEdgesBoundingBox().GetWidth()) boardHeight = pcbnew.ToMM(self.board.GetBoardEdgesBoundingBox().GetHeight()) if hasattr(self.board, 'GetCopperLayerCount'): boardLayer = self.board.GetCopperLayerCount() gerberData = {'boardWidth':boardWidth,'boardHeight':boardHeight,'boardLayer':boardLayer} return gerberData def get_name(self): p_name = self.board.GetFileName() return p_name def parse_attrs(self, attrs): return {} if not isinstance(attrs, int) else { 'tht': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, pcbnew.FP_THROUGH_HOLE), 'smd': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, pcbnew.FP_SMD), 'not_in_pos': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, Part No.', 'Mfg Part'] for key in keys: try: if f.HasField(key): return f.GetFieldByName(key).GetText() except Exception as e: if f.HasProperty(key): return f.GetProperty(key) def get_pack_from_footprint(self, f): keys = ['pack', 'PACK', 'Pack', 'package' ,'PACKAGE', 'Package', 'case', 'CASE', 'Case'] for key in keys: try: if f.HasField(key): return f.GetFieldByName(key).GetText() except Exception as e: if f.HasProperty(key): return f.GetProperty(key) def parse_attr_flag(self, attr, mask): return mask == (attr & mask) Upload photo 0 /10000 You can upload up to 5 images! Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Join us Wanna be a dedicated PCBWay writer? We definately look forward to having you with us. Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Besides, PCBWay will continue to enhance its manufacturing capabilities to bring more choices and personalized services to customers in the future. Verify Now Blog > HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design by: Mila Sep 03,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout hdi pcb HDI pcb design optical module pcb high speed pcb layout An optical module PCB is a typical high-frequency, high-density HDI PCB precision board. Its material selection is closely related to transmission rate, link length, loss budget, and device platforms. While 10G and lower modules can use materials like high-Tg FR-4, high-speed modules operating at 25G, 56G, 100G, 400G, and 800G impose stringent requirements on low-loss materials, impedance control, and manufacturing consistency. Below are seven core layout design points and key differences compared to standard PCBs, focusing on high speed pcb layout and practical signal integrity engineering without rigid design fallacies. 1. Substrate Selection and StackUp Design Substrate selection and layer stackup form the foundation for stable high-frequency transmission, directly determining link insertion loss, impedance accuracy, and signal integrity. Multi-Dimensional Rate-Matched Selection: For 25G+ channels, select substrates considering Nyquist frequency, link length, insertion loss budget, dielectric loss, copper foil roughness, and stackup. For long-distance or low-loss channels, choose mid-to-low loss high-speed substrates. Non-critical areas like low-speed control and power can use high-Tg FR-4 to balance performance and cost on an optical module PCB. Adjacent Reference Ground Planes: High-speed differential signal layers should adopt a "signal-reference ground" structure to minimize edge-field coupling. Power layers should pair with adjacent ground layers to optimize PDN impedance via inter-layer capacitance. Pre-Simulation Impedance Modeling: Determine stackup parameters early through SI simulation. The industry standard target is typically 100 ohms differential impedance, with high-performance channels strictly controlling tolerances within +/- 5%. 2. High-Speed Differential TX/RX Signal Integrity High-speed differential signals are the core of data transmission in an optical module PCB. Design should focus on eliminating geometric discontinuities and parasitic interference. Symmetry and Equal Length: Match trace widths, spacing, bends, and via layouts for differential pairs. Advanced HDI pcb design requires controlling intra-pair length skew to prevent differential-to-common mode noise conversion. Trace Geometry Continuity: Use 45-degree angles or smooth arc transitions instead of rigid 90-degree turns. High-frequency reflections stem mostly from vias, pads, stubs, and split reference planes rather than standard trace corners. Minimal Via Structures and Stub Optimization: Minimize layer transitions. For long through-hole structures, apply back-drilling to remove residual stubs, cutting down reflections and resonances. （Backdrill + Via Stub） Unbroken High-Frequency Return Paths: Avoid routing differential traces across ground splits or slot gaps. Provide nearby stitching ground vias whenever signals switch layers. (Differential Pair + Reference Plane + Return Path) Crosstalk Mitigation: Apply the 3W rule during initial layout for proper spacing. For 112G PAM4 ultra-high-speed scenarios, refine trace spacing with 3D EM simulation and add ground via shielding walls where necessary. 3. Optoelectronic Isolation and Sensitive Layout Optical modules combine sensitive analog signals with high-speed digital logic. The analog front-end requires isolation from power and digital noise. Physical Isolation: Separate TOSA/ROSA components and TIA analog circuits from high-speed digital traces and switching power supplies based on form factors (SFP, QSFP, OSFP). Short Analog Traces: Keep weak analog traces from optical devices to TIA and driver ICs as short as possible, avoiding parallel routing alongside high-speed digital lines. Analog Circuit Shielding: Implement localized ground shielding or small metal shields around laser drivers and TIA circuits to isolate high-frequency digital noise. 4. Power Integrity (PI) Optimization Focus on low-impedance return paths, minimal current loops, and sub-region noise reduction. Minimal Loop Decoupling: Configure decoupling networks based on target PDN impedance. Place capacitors close to power pins to minimize parasitic inductance. Solid Ground Plane Priority: Maintain a continuous, low-impedance ground plane across the HDI PCB to provide a solid reference. Apply localized filtering for sensitive analog zones rather than single-point star grounding across the board. Thermal Copper Pour for Power Chips: Place large copper areas with thermal via arrays beneath heat-generating components like laser drivers to disperse heat quickly. 5. Thermal Management in HDI PCB Design Optical module DSPs, optical drivers, and laser diodes generate concentrated heat. High temperatures cause device aging, DK/Df parameter drift, and impedance shifts. Efficient Thermal Paths: Place dense thermal via arrays under high-power devices (DSP, TOSA) to transfer heat from the optical module PCB inner layers to the metal housing. Hot/Cold Component Partitioning: Isolate heat sources from temperature-sensitive optical and clock components to prevent thermal drift and premature aging. Symmetrical Design against Warpage: Balance copper distribution and layer stack-ups across the HDI PCB to manage thermal-mechanical stress during reflow soldering. （Thermal Path IC → Thermal Via → Copper Plane → Housing） 6. EMC and Grounding for High Speed PCB Layout Symmetrical Routing for Common-Mode Noise: Maintain structural symmetry in high-speed differential traces to reduce EMI radiation. Connect the module metal shell to the PCB ground for low-impedance shielding. Interface ESD Protection : Place TVS diodes and common-mode chokes near edge connectors to route ESD currents quickly to chassis ground. Isolate Interference Sources: Keep power inductors and switching regulators away from sensitive RX analog inputs to prevent magnetic coupling. 7. DFM Guidelines for Optical Module PCB Manufacturing Precise HDI pcb design and assembly standards ensure manufacturing yield for dense components. Precision Soldering Design: Use Via-in-Pad or micro-vias for high-density BGAs. For QFN thermal pads, use segmented stencil openings to reduce solder voiding and floating. Optical Alignment Tolerance: Match mechanical outline and mounting hole tolerances precisely with metal housings to avoid optical misalignments. Test Points and Gold Fingers: Keep test points off high-speed trunk lines. Use hard gold plating for edge connector gold fingers to ensure durability across insertion cycles. 8.Optical Module PCB vs Standard PCB Core Differences Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design HDI PCB Layout Guide for High Speed Optical Module PCB Design by: Mila Sep 03,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout hdi pcb HDI pcb design optical module pcb high speed pcb layout An optical module PCB is a typical high-frequency, high-density HDI PCB precision board. Its material selection is closely related to transmission rate, link length, loss budget, and device platforms. While 10G and lower modules can use materials like high-Tg FR-4, high-speed modules operating at 25G, 56G, 100G, 400G, and 800G impose stringent requirements on low-loss materials, impedance control, and manufacturing consistency. Below are seven core layout design points and key differences compared to standard PCBs, focusing on high speed pcb layout and practical signal integrity engineering without rigid design fallacies. 1. Substrate Selection and StackUp Design Substrate selection and layer stackup form the foundation for stable high-frequency transmission, directly determining link insertion loss, impedance accuracy, and signal integrity. Multi-Dimensional Rate-Matched Selection: For 25G+ channels, select substrates considering Nyquist frequency, link length, insertion loss budget, dielectric loss, copper foil roughness, and stackup. For long-distance or low-loss channels, choose mid-to-low loss high-speed substrates. Non-critical areas like low-speed control and power can use high-Tg FR-4 to balance performance and cost on an optical module PCB. Adjacent Reference Ground Planes: High-speed differential signal layers should adopt a "signal-reference ground" structure to minimize edge-field coupling. Power layers should pair with adjacent ground layers to optimize PDN impedance via inter-layer capacitance. Pre-Simulation Impedance Modeling: Determine stackup parameters early through SI simulation. The industry standard target is typically 100 ohms differential impedance, with high-performance channels strictly controlling tolerances within +/- 5%. 2. High-Speed Differential TX/RX Signal Integrity High-speed differential signals are the core of data transmission in an optical module PCB. Design should focus on eliminating geometric discontinuities and parasitic interference. Symmetry and Equal Length: Match trace widths, spacing, bends, and via layouts for differential pairs. Advanced HDI pcb design requires controlling intra-pair length skew to prevent differential-to-common mode noise conversion. Trace Geometry Continuity: Use 45-degree angles or smooth arc transitions instead of rigid 90-degree turns. High-frequency reflections stem mostly from vias, pads, stubs, and split reference planes rather than standard trace corners. Minimal Via Structures and Stub Optimization: Minimize layer transitions. For long through-hole structures, apply back-drilling to remove residual stubs, cutting down reflections and resonances. （Backdrill + Via Stub） Unbroken High-Frequency Return Paths: Avoid routing differential traces across ground splits or slot gaps. Provide nearby stitching ground vias whenever signals switch layers. (Differential Pair + Reference Plane + Return Path) Crosstalk Mitigation: Apply the 3W rule during initial layout for proper spacing. For 112G PAM4 ultra-high-speed scenarios, refine trace spacing with 3D EM simulation and add ground via shielding walls where necessary. 3. Optoelectronic Isolation and Sensitive Layout Optical modules combine sensitive analog signals with high-speed digital logic. The analog front-end requires isolation from power and digital noise. Physical Isolation: Separate TOSA/ROSA components and TIA analog circuits from high-speed digital traces and switching power supplies based on form factors (SFP, QSFP, OSFP). Short Analog Traces: Keep weak analog traces from optical devices to TIA and driver ICs as short as possible, avoiding parallel routing alongside high-speed digital lines. Analog Circuit Shielding: Implement localized ground shielding or small metal shields around laser drivers and TIA circuits to isolate high-frequency digital noise. 4. Power Integrity (PI) Optimization Focus on low-impedance return paths, minimal current loops, and sub-region noise reduction. Minimal Loop Decoupling: Configure decoupling networks based on target PDN impedance. Place capacitors close to power pins to minimize parasitic inductance. Solid Ground Plane Priority: Maintain a continuous, low-impedance ground plane across the HDI PCB to provide a solid reference. Apply localized filtering for sensitive analog zones rather than single-point star grounding across the board. Thermal Copper Pour for Power Chips: Place large copper areas with thermal via arrays beneath heat-generating components like laser drivers to disperse heat quickly. 5. Thermal Management in HDI PCB Design Optical module DSPs, optical drivers, and laser diodes generate concentrated heat. High temperatures cause device aging, DK/Df parameter drift, and impedance shifts. Efficient Thermal Paths: Place dense thermal via arrays under high-power devices (DSP, TOSA) to transfer heat from the optical module PCB inner layers to the metal housing. Hot/Cold Component Partitioning: Isolate heat sources from temperature-sensitive optical and clock components to prevent thermal drift and premature aging. Symmetrical Design against Warpage: Balance copper distribution and layer stack-ups across the HDI PCB to manage thermal-mechanical stress during reflow soldering. （Thermal Path IC → Thermal Via → Copper Plane → Housing） 6. EMC and Grounding for High Speed PCB Layout Symmetrical Routing for Common-Mode Noise: Maintain structural symmetry in high-speed differential traces to reduce EMI radiation. Connect the module metal shell to the PCB ground for low-impedance shielding. Interface ESD Protection : Place TVS diodes and common-mode chokes near edge connectors to route ESD currents quickly to chassis ground. Isolate Interference Sources: Keep power inductors and switching regulators away from sensitive RX analog inputs to prevent magnetic coupling. 7. DFM Guidelines for Optical Module PCB Manufacturing Precise HDI pcb design and assembly standards ensure manufacturing yield for dense components. Precision Soldering Design: Use Via-in-Pad or micro-vias for high-density BGAs. For QFN thermal pads, use segmented stencil openings to reduce solder voiding and floating. Optical Alignment Tolerance: Match mechanical outline and mounting hole tolerances precisely with metal housings to avoid optical misalignments. Test Points and Gold Fingers: Keep test points off high-speed trunk lines. Use hard gold plating for edge connector gold fingers to ensure durability across insertion cycles. 8.Optical Module PCB vs Standard PCB Core Differences Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > High-Speed ADC PCB Layout Guide: EPAD, PDS, and Grounding Best Practices High-Speed ADC PCB Layout Guide: EPAD, PDS, and Grounding Best Practices by: Mila Sep 10,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout high speed analog to digital converter high speed adc adc layout adc pcb design High-speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC) PCB layout involves multiple design parameters, and their importance varies depending on the application. For high-speed ADC systems, the focus should not be on optimizing every routing detail, but on avoiding common design deviations and maintaining the overall performance of the signal chain. For a broader overview of PCB Layout principles, designers should also consider signal integrity, power integrity, grounding, and return paths as part of the overall design. 1. EPAD Design Guidelines for ADC PCB Design The exposed pad (EPAD), defined as Pin 0 by ADI, is the core pad located on the bottom of many integrated circuit packages. It typically provides the main grounding and thermal connection and serves as an important path for the internal ground structure. Some converters and amplifiers do not have dedicated ground pins, with their grounding function primarily relying on the EPAD. Therefore, EPAD design directly affects electrical connection stability and thermal performance and should not be overlooked in ADC PCB design. The EPAD must form a reliable solder connection with the PCB to ensure both electrical and thermal connectivity. Poor soldering or insufficient contact can lead to abnormal grounding, inadequate heat dissipation, and even malfunction of the signal chain. For reliable EPAD performance, three key aspects should be considered in ADC PCB design. Multilayer Grounding and Thermal Copper According to the device datasheet and overall thermal requirements, grounding and thermal copper structures can be added on the appropriate PCB layers. These structures should provide reliable electrical and thermal connections to the PCB ground planes, helping improve heat dissipation, particularly in high-power and multichannel signal-chain applications. The bottom layer can also incorporate a corresponding grounding or thermal area when required by the device and system design. Depending on the application, this area can support grounding, thermal management, high-frequency decoupling, or mechanical positioning for a bottom-side thermal structure. （exposed pad pcb design） EPAD Pad Segmentation A large EPAD can be divided into multiple smaller areas using a cross-hatched stencil pattern or solder mask segmentation. During reflow soldering, solder paste distribution can vary across a large continuous pad, potentially resulting in uneven soldering, voids, or insufficient effective contact. Proper EPAD segmentation helps improve solder paste distribution and create a more uniform and stable connection between the device and PCB, improving both electrical and thermal reliability. EPAD Ground Vias and Via Filling Ground vias can be added to individual EPAD sections according to the device recommendations and PCB manufacturing requirements. Whether these vias require solder paste filling, epoxy filling, or other treatment depends on the via dimensions, pad structure, and manufacturing process. For via structures that may allow solder paste to flow into the holes during reflow, appropriate via filling or solder mask treatment should be considered. This helps reduce soldering defects and improves the reliability of the EPAD electrical and thermal connection. (EPAD design: large vs segmented) 2. Power Decoupling and PDS Design for High-Speed ADC The primary goal of PCB power decoupling is to reduce the impedance of the power delivery system (PDS) to ground. A common mistake is to place large numbers of capacitors with different capacitance values without considering their actual frequency response. In practice, a large number of redundant capacitors is not always necessary. Carefully selecting capacitors based on capacitance, component type, package, and process characteristics can optimize PDS impedance while saving PCB space and reducing component cost. Redundant capacitors can introduce layout congestion, additional cost, and potential resonance risks. They do not inherently violate PCB manufacturing requirements, but excessive or poorly planned decoupling can reduce overall design efficiency. Capacitor Selection and PCB Decoupling Layout The performance of a capacitor varies with its package and construction. Even capacitors from the same supplier can have different frequency responses depending on package size, process, and component type. Therefore, there is no universal frequency limit for capacitor decoupling performance. The effective frequency range depends on package size, equivalent series inductance (ESL), component characteristics, and the actual PCB layout. If capacitor selection or placement is inappropriate, multiple capacitors can introduce additional inductive loops. Capacitors with different parameters may also resonate at specific frequencies, potentially increasing rather than reducing PDS impedance. Capacitor frequency-response characteristics should therefore be considered before placement and selection. （ADC decoupling capacitor layout） 3. High-Frequency PDS and PCB Stackup Design The effective decoupling range of discrete capacitors depends on their electrical characteristics and PCB layout, and there is no universal high-frequency cutoff. As frequency increases, package parasitics and ESL increasingly limit the high-frequency performance of discrete capacitors. At higher frequencies, the intrinsic capacitance formed between PCB power and ground planes becomes an important part of PDS design. Proper stackup design can therefore complement conventional discrete decoupling. Six-Layer PCB Stackup A typical six-layer PCB stackup can be arranged as: Top Signal → Ground 1 → Power 1 → Power 2 → Ground 2 → Bottom Signal In high-speed PCB design, keeping the dielectric thickness between adjacent power and ground planes relatively small, such as a typical range of 2–4 mil, helps increase plane capacitance and reduce the impedance of high-frequency current paths. This optimization is achieved primarily through the PCB stackup and does not require additional components. The required stackup and dielectric thickness simply need to be specified in the PCB fabrication documentation. Eight-Layer PCB Stackup Optimization For an eight-layer PCB, additional ground reference layers can be introduced while maintaining a small core-layer spacing, such as 2–3 mil. This can significantly increase the intrinsic plane capacitance, although the actual increase is not necessarily double. It depends on dielectric thickness, copper area, and the overall configuration of the power and ground layers. Compared with simply adding more high-frequency discrete capacitors, stackup optimization can reduce component count and provide a cleaner high-frequency PDS structure. PDS Impedance and Dynamic Current The primary function of the PDS is to suppress voltage fluctuations caused by the dynamic current demand of the circuit. Low-impedance power and ground planes, combined with an appropriate PCB stackup, can reduce voltage fluctuations caused by rapidly changing currents. According to V = IR, if the dynamic current is 1 A and the PDS impedance is 10 mΩ, the corresponding voltage variation is approximately 10 mV. Optimizing the PCB stackup can extend the effective high-frequency low-impedance range, but overall PDS performance is also affected by power-plane integrity, ground-via placement, package parasitics, and local current-loop design. Therefore, conventional low-frequency decoupling capacitors can be placed at key locations such as power-entry points, high-power devices, and surge-current devices. Combining different decoupling mechanisms can help optimize PDS impedance over a broad frequency range. Dense capacitor placement around every IC is not always necessary and may introduce unnecessary cost, space consumption, and resonance risks. （discrete vs plane capacitance） 4. PCB Layer-to-Layer Coupling and Noise Suppression In multilayer PCB layouts, sensitive analog layers, including analog power, ground, and signal layers, can experience crosstalk when placed close to high-frequency digital layers. Because some noise sources are located directly above or below sensitive analog layers, this type of coupling can easily be overlooked. Layer Coupling in ADC Layout Adjacent PCB conductor layers form parasitic capacitive structures, which can produce electric-field coupling under certain frequency and layout conditions. The actual coupling level has no fixed value and depends on factors such as layer spacing, dielectric thickness, copper area, routing length, signal edge rate, return path, and interlayer parasitic capacitance. For example, if simulation or measurement confirms that a high-speed digital signal produces approximately 1 mV of interference at a sensitive analog node through layer coupling, this interference corresponds to about 2 LSB for a 12-bit ADC with a 2 Vpp full-scale range and about 8 LSB for a 14-bit ADC. In high-resolution ADC systems, such coupling can significantly reduce signal margin and system SNR. Therefore, during ADC layout, the signal characteristics of adjacent layers should be carefully evaluated. High-noise digital layers should be kept away from sensitive analog layers where practical, while appropriate stackup, routing, and return-path design should be used to reduce interlayer coupling. 5. Analog and Digital Grounding in ADC PCB Design In ADC PCB design, there is no universal requirement to divide the ground plane into analog ground (AGND) and digital ground (DGND). The appropriate approach depends on the device manufacturer's recommendations, system partitioning, and current return paths. In many conventional applications, a continuous ground plane is preferable to unnecessary segmentation. （Backflow Path） Why Avoid Unnecessary Ground Plane Splitting? Unnecessary ground-plane splitting can increase the inductance of current return paths. According to V = L(di/dt), higher return-path inductance increases transient voltage noise caused by rapidly changing currents and may also worsen the high-frequency impedance characteristics of the local power and ground network. As ADC sampling rates increase, switching currents can change more rapidly, making parasitic inductance in the return path increasingly important. Therefore, a continuous ground plane should generally be maintained unless system requirements indicate otherwise. Optimize ADC Return Paths Through Functional Partitioning The core of grounding design is functional partitioning and return-path optimization. By separating analog and digital circuits through appropriate component placement and controlling the return paths of high-speed digital signals, unwanted interaction between analog and digital sections can be reduced. In many applications, proper PCB layout, a continuous ground reference plane, and controlled return paths can provide good grounding performance without physically splitting the ground plane. Should AGND and DGND Be Connected at a Single Point? Ground-plane segmentation may be considered when layout constraints prevent effective functional partitioning or when high-noise digital circuits and power buses cannot be sufficiently separated from sensitive analog circuitry. However, a single-point AGND-DGND connection is not universally appropriate for every ADC system. The grounding method should be selected based on device characteristics, PCB return-path distribution, and overall system noise performance, with the device datasheet and system requirements serving as the primary references. 6. High-Speed ADC Layout Design Summary High-speed ADC layout should focus on the key factors that directly affect signal-chain performance rather than adding unnecessary design complexity. For system-level, module-level, and evaluation-board designs, a continuous ground plane can generally be preferred, with functional partitioning used to optimize return paths and reduce layer-to-layer coupling. PCB assembly processes can also directly affect system performance. Manufacturing documentation should specify EPAD segmentation, via treatment, and other relevant assembly requirements according to the device and manufacturing process to ensure reliable solder connections. Power decoupling should be based on accurate component selection and targeted placement. Combined with a PCB stackup that places power and ground planes closely together, this approach can improve high-frequency decoupling performance. Conventional low-frequency decoupling capacitors can then be used at appropriate locations to optimize PDS impedance over a broad frequency range. For high-speed analog-to-digital converter applications, ADC PCB design should be adapted to the specific system requirements. A well-planned ADC layout should focus on device connectivity, power integrity, high-frequency impedance, layer-to-layer coupling, and grounding and return paths. By addressing these factors together, designers can improve the stability and overall performance of high-speed ADC systems. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac.
